posts.title: Entering the Next Frontier: Unreal Engine 5
posts.excerpt: We're proud to announce that Sirius Reborn is now being developed on Unreal Engine 5. Next-gen visuals, dynamic lighting, and vast open-world possibilities await.
posts.body:
We're proud to announce that **Sirius Reborn is now being developed on Unreal Engine 5**.

When we started this project, the goal was simple: bring the Sirius sector back with the look and feel players remember, but with the technology it always deserved. Moving to Unreal Engine 5 is the biggest step toward that goal so far.

## What the switch gives us

- **Lumen dynamic lighting.** Stars, nebulae and docking bays now light ships in real time. Flying out of a station's shadow into open sunlight finally feels like it should.
- **Nanite geometry.** Capital ships, stations and asteroid fields can carry far more detail without us hand-building a dozen LODs for every model.
- **World Partition.** Each system streams in as you fly, which keeps load screens to jump gates and docking only.
- **Niagara.** Engine trails, cruise effects and weapon fire are being rebuilt from scratch on the new particle system.

## What stays the same

The flight model, the economy and the story beats of the original are our reference. If something felt right in 2003, we want it to feel right here too: just sharper, brighter and bigger.

More technical deep dives are coming. Thanks for flying with us.

posts.title: Capital Ships & Scale in Sirius Reborn
posts.excerpt: A first look at the next-generation capital ship technology. Massive scale, detailed modeling, and cinematic presentation like never before.
posts.body:
A first look at our next-generation capital ship pipeline.

In the original game, battleships and cruisers were imposing, but the hardware of the day limited how close you could get before the illusion broke. In Sirius Reborn, capital ships are built to be inspected up close.

## Real scale

Every capital ship is modelled at true scale relative to fighters. A Liberty dreadnought now dwarfs your ship the way it always did in your imagination, with turret batteries, hangar bays and running lights you can fly between.

## Detail where it counts

With Nanite we can keep hull plating, greebles and damage decals on the model itself instead of faking them with textures. Damage is persistent across a fight, so a long engagement leaves its scars.

## Cinematic presentation

Docking approaches, jump gate transits and fleet arrivals get dedicated camera work. They're short and skippable, but they sell the size of the universe you're flying in.

We'll share more on individual ship classes in upcoming updates.

posts.title: Rebuilding Liberty: Planets and Colonies
posts.excerpt: Exploring the visual and technical overhaul of iconic locations. From Planet Manhattan to the far edges of Sirius.
posts.body:
Exploring the visual and technical overhaul of the sector's most iconic locations.

## Planets that feel like places

Planets in Sirius Reborn get layered atmospheres, cloud cover with real-time shadowing and city lights on the night side. Manhattan's sprawl is visible from orbit, and the approach to a landing zone now reads as descending into a living world.

## Bases and stations

Every base is being rebuilt from the original layouts as a reference. We keep the silhouettes you know and replace the low-poly interiors with fully lit hangars, bars and equipment dealers.

## The edges of Sirius

Beyond the house worlds, the frontier systems get the same treatment: ice fields with volumetric fog, radiation clouds that actually obscure your view and debris fields you'll want to fly slowly through.

Next up: a closer look at how we light nebulae.

posts.title: Combat Reimagined: Weapons & Effects
posts.excerpt: Next-gen weapon effects, particle systems, and space combat feedback powered by Niagara and Chaos Physics.
posts.body:
Next-generation weapon effects, particle systems and combat feedback, powered by Niagara and Chaos Physics.

## Every gun has a voice

Lasers, particle cannons, plasma and tachyon weapons each get distinct projectiles, muzzle flashes, impact effects and audio. You should be able to tell what's shooting at you without looking at the target panel.

## Impacts with weight

Shield hits ripple across the bubble around a ship; hull hits throw sparks and debris. Chaos Physics drives wreckage, so destroyed ships break apart in pieces that drift, tumble and collide.

## Readable combat

Effects are bright, but readability comes first. Hit markers, shield and hull feedback and missile warnings are tuned so the screen never turns into noise during a dogfight.

Expect gameplay footage once the first combat build is stable.
